text:
morgan: Quick heads-up — targeting tonight's publish window 21:00 PT for Python and TS SDKs. Need final agreement on pin strategy and the vendored-compat shim rollout. CI currently green but one flaky e2e in canary.

sam: What's the exact rollback criteria? If the canary fails runtime errors we roll back immediately, or do we hotfix?

karim: Agree rollback on any runtime exception in sync client (esp signer mismatch) for >3% of canary requests. For docs-only regressions we can roll forward with patch.

release-bot: publish-job 2026-07-09T04:10: queued -> running. Staging build artifacts: packages/sdk-py-2.1.0rc1.tar.gz, packages/sdk-ts-2.1.0-rc1.tgz

morgan: Flagging two deployment ops: (1) push npm & pypi packages (2) update deprecation banner for legacy sync client and add compat shim toggle.

lina: Compat shim is a small vendored adapter so users on old sync API don't break. Ops question: do we ship shim behind a feature flag or enable by default for a week?

sam: Prefer behind flag `compat_sync_v2` default ON for 48h, then OFF by default but with opt-in for a month. That limits blast radius.

ci-bot: e2e/canary had 1 failed test: test_chat_integration::test_kv_cache_eviction — flake detected earlier 2026-06-28. Rerun queued.

karim: If rerun passes, proceed. If it fails again, hold publish and run bisect on runtime image/kernel selection. We don't want to release with a caching bug.

morgan: Publishing commands for ops reference: `npm publish packages/sdk-ts-2.1.0-rc1.tgz --tag canary` and `python -m twine upload dist/sdk_py-2.1.0rc1.tar.gz --repository pypi --config-file .pypirc`

morgan: Also planning a short release note blurb for deprecation: "The legacy sync client (v1.x) will be deprecated; please migrate to the async-first client by 2026-09-01. A compat shim is provided to ease transition; opt-out instructions included."

sam: Add explicit rollback steps in the release notes: how to pin to previous pinned versions and npm unpublish steps if necessary. Example: `npm install @redwood/sdk@2.0.7 --save-exact` and `pip install redwood-sdk==2.0.7`

release-bot: canary traffic split applied: 5% -> sdk-ts:2.1.0-rc1, 5% -> sdk-py:2.1.0rc1; remaining traffic -> 2.0.x

lina: QA will run smoke on staging with the compat flag toggled off then on, please wait for approval from @karim and @sam before promoting to stable tag.

ci-bot: rerun results: e2e/canary passed 3/3. No new flake reproduction.

karim: Given rerun pass, okay to proceed with staged publish. Ops: push RC to `canary` tags, monitor logs for signer mismatch and 5xx rates. If 5xx > 0.5% for 10m we trigger rollback.

morgan: I'll post the release notes draft to docs PR and update console rollout config to start 2am UTC gradual increase to 30% over 2 hours.

sam: Reminder to coordinate with support for canned responses and to update in-app deprecation banner. Also add a short blurb to the status page in case of rollback.

release-bot: publish-job completed: artifacts uploaded and canary tags set. Telemetry hooks active.

lina: QA ✅. I sign off to promote to stable tag when ops increase traffic to 30%.

morgan: Promote plan executed at 21:40 PT -> updating npm/pypi tags to `latest`. Sending deprecation email to beta cohort tomorrow.

karim: Monitor dashboards for 30m. If anything abnormal ping #eng-oncall and call immediate rollback.

sam: Noted. If we rollback, use `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@2.0.7 latest` and `twine upload` old release re-tag steps, and revert compat flag to previous default.

morgan: Thanks everyone — I'll open a follow-up thread with post-release checklist and final changelog entry. :rocket:

ci-bot: post-deploy checks 10m: error-rate 0.11%, latency P95 +3ms, signer errors 0.0% -> healthy.

morgan: Closing thread — final artifacts published and deprecation banner scheduled.
